# macOS computer Runner

Terra (`gpt-6.1-terra`, low reasoning, implicit cache enabled) operates a local macOS
app through its native computer tool. Appium 3.9.0 and Mac2 4.5.1 execute the
mouse/keyboard actions and capture screenshots. Fresh Accessibility XML is an
optional read tool; incomplete AX does not prevent coordinate input.

## Public Node API

```js
import { run } from "@katalon-loki/mac-computer-runner";
const result = await run(
  {
    requestId: "unique-request",
    scenarioId: "sample-suite",
    scenario:
      "Create a sample project, run one of its test suites, and view the execution result.",
    params: {
      "Project name": "Example project",
      "Project location": "/Users/example/Projects",
      "Sample project": "Sample API Tests Project",
    },
    target: { app: "com.kms.katalon.product.product", launch: true },
  },
  {
    apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY,
    artifactDirectory: "/absolute/private/empty/directory",
    signal: controller.signal,
    limits: { calls: 80, desktopInputs: 150, ms: 600000 },
  },
);
```

Always provide the full scenario and explicit params (`{}` when empty). IDs only
correlate evidence. App is a bundle ID, never an executable command. `launch:false`
requires an already-running app; otherwise Appium may launch it. Existing app
state is preserved at startup and the app stays open after execution/Stop.

## Plugin

Use the existing `loki_runner_execute`, `loki_runner_get`, and `loki_runner_stop`
with `executionMethod:"desktop-ui"` and the desktop target above. The worker imports
this package directly. Browser execution remains `browser-ui` with `initialURL`.
No additional MCP server, Peekaboo installation or global Appium installation is
required. The plugin packages the pinned dependency graph and uses its bundled Node.

## Host requirements and lifecycle

- macOS with an unlocked GUI and a configured full Xcode installation, including
  accepted Xcode license/first-launch components. Runner uses the host
  `DEVELOPER_DIR`, active Xcode, or `/Applications/Xcode.app` when only Command Line
  Tools are selected. It does not change the system developer directory.
- Grant Apple's UI Automation prompt and Accessibility permission to the
  WebDriverAgent/Xcode helper when prompted. These grants are host setup, not
  model actions. An unavailable session/capture stops before the first paid call.
- The first invocation builds WebDriverAgent using Xcode. Writable build/cache
  state lives under `~/Library/Caches/kaijan/mac-runner`, outside the installed
  plugin. Appium is loopback-only on a fresh port; no relaxed-security features,
  AppleScript, model-generated code or external Appium server are exposed.
- One Runner controls the desktop at a time. A local OS socket lease on port
  52841 prevents concurrent runs and is released on process death. A busy port
  blocks execution; Runner does not kill its owner.
- Screenshots cover the **main display**, including native menus and dialogs.
  Keep the target on that display. A small fixed, read-only CoreGraphics helper
  reports display bounds; Appium supplies the screenshot. Recorded geometry maps
  screenshot pixels to global screen points without a fixed Retina scale.
- The API supports click/right-click/double-click, hover, typing, keypresses,
  scrolling and two-point drag. A longer curved drag or middle click is reported
  as unsupported, never silently changed to another input. Meta and Control
  remain distinct; no shortcut preference is injected into the scenario.
- Stop aborts pending requests, prevents subsequent input and cleans up owned
  Appium/WebDriverAgent processes. A dispatched input may already have taken
  effect; an interrupted command is not retried automatically.

## Evidence and limits

Private output contains request/response and HTTP receipts, calls, structured
browser-independent actions, screenshots and display geometry, optional AX reads,
Appium logs, cleanup receipt, manifest and result. Parameters appear in the private
initial request; reported action/result text redacts declared secret values.
Screenshots/raw provider evidence can contain secrets and must not be published.
Native execution has no Playwright trace: its journal, screenshots and Appium logs
are the corresponding diagnostic evidence.

`executionState:"completed"` means Terra stopped issuing actions. `testVerdict`
remains `unverified`; its final answer is a model claim, not independent business
verification. Results include calls, desktop inputs, token usage, estimated USD,
USD per 10,000 inputs and requests with missing usage. Unknown charges are excluded
from the estimate. Failed attempts must not be compared as successful executions.

No JEV, memory saving, replay learning, business-outcome review or provider retry is
added. Missing AX, external provider errors and unsupported commands remain visible.

Reference: [Mac2 capabilities](https://appium.github.io/appium-mac2-driver/latest/reference/capabilities/).
